correctness.rationale: Exact equations (1),(2) are the sum and difference of two parity-shifted recurrence equations and hence are jointly necessary and sufficient. All same-positive, same-negative, mixed-sign and zero cases are examined. For odd k the determinant a^2+sh is positive; for even k, its potentially vanishing counterpart a^2-sh is checked in the unsolved system, yielding 0=2 and no missed cycle. Strict sign inequalities yield uniqueness and thresholds. The three divergent/finite boundary laws are algebraic consequences of the explicit formulas. The self-contained standard-library checker passed 18,150 exact rational nonsingular case comparisons and three singular-line examples. These checks do not replace the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The full defining preprint supplies the arbitrary-delay recurrence, fixed points and stability regions, but not the all-delay parity two-cycle classification. Botella-Soler et al. explicitly cover the planar (k,d)=(1,2) formulas and bisecting lines, which are conceded. The verified new comparison is the universal k-even/d-odd existence threshold max(nu,sqrt(nu(2-nu))) with a two-sided infinity pole at nu<1, one-sided pole at nu=1 and finite negative continuum at nu>1, plus the complete parity census. The inspected orientation-preserving planar Lozi itinerary theorem does not cover arbitrary delays. The literature/record searches do not certify priority, but no covering statement was found. Unindexed equivalences remain a real risk.
residual_risks: A nonindexed or untranslated paper could contain an equivalent parity classification; search coverage does not prove priority.

value.rationale: The model was introduced to study delay-dependent high-dimensional bifurcations; the complete least-two orbit census for every pair of integer delays is a natural structural invariant. The sharp threshold for k even and d odd produces a phase-dependent two-sided pole, one-sided pole or finite continuum, not a routine restatement of the known classical planar case. It exhibits an actual period-two orbit {2,-6} before any negative fixed point exists, and mean phase sign is governed solely by nonlinear delay parity. This gives a testable obstruction to extrapolating planar Lozi bifurcation diagrams to higher delay dimensions, without claiming attractor stability.
